scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Grant to the Institutions for Long Term Project in the Field of Art and Culture (Sarjansheel Goa)
description:
The Scheme to Provide Grant to the Institutions for Long Term Project in the Field of Art and Culture is also known as Sarjansheel Goa.

This scheme was launched by the Government of Goa in the year 2019.

The primary objective of Sarjansheel Goa is to promote and preserve the rich cultural heritage of Goa.

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to various institutions involved in long-term projects related to art and culture.

The government has set a measurable target of supporting at least 10 institutions annually under this scheme.

The total budget allocation for Sarjansheel Goa is approximately ₹5 crore per year.

Each selected institution can receive a grant ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹50 lakh.

The grant amount is determined based on the scope and scale of the proposed project.

Eligible projects may include those related to traditional art forms, music, dance, theater, and literature.

The scheme also encourages projects that promote local artisans and craftsmen.

Institutions applying for the grant must be registered under the Societies Registration Act of 1860 or similar legislation.

The eligibility criteria specify that the institutions should have been operational for a minimum of three years.

Institutions must demonstrate a track record of successful projects in the field of art and culture.

The application process involves submitting a detailed project proposal to the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa.

The proposal must include a project description, objectives, timeline, and budget breakdown.

Applicants are required to provide proof of registration and a list of governing body members.

The deadline for submitting applications is usually set for the end of the financial year, specifically March 31.

Once applications are received, they are reviewed by a committee formed by the Directorate of Art and Culture.

The review process typically takes about two months.

Successful applicants are notified by the end of May each year.

Funds are disbursed in two installments.

The first installment is released upon approval of the project.

The second installment is contingent upon the submission of progress reports and utilization certificates.

Institutions must complete their projects within a stipulated timeframe of one to two years.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa.

The Directorate can be contacted via their official website or through their office located in Panaji.

The contact number for the Directorate of Art and Culture is +91 832 222 4200.

The scheme aims to enhance the visibility of Goan art and culture on national and international platforms.

It also seeks to foster collaboration between various cultural institutions and artists.

The scheme encourages innovative projects that can attract tourism to Goa.

Projects that involve community participation are given preference.

The government emphasizes the importance of sustainability in the projects funded under this scheme.

Institutions must ensure that their projects have a lasting impact on the community.

The scheme also supports research and documentation of traditional art forms.

Institutions are encouraged to organize workshops and training sessions as part of their projects.

The Sarjansheel Goa scheme aligns with the broader cultural policies of the Government of India.

It complements initiatives such as the National Mission on Cultural Mapping.

The scheme is part of Goa's efforts to promote its unique cultural identity.

The government aims to create a vibrant cultural ecosystem through this initiative.

The scheme also recognizes the contributions of local artists and cultural practitioners.

It provides a platform for emerging artists to showcase their work.

Institutions are required to submit a final report upon project completion.

The final report must detail the outcomes and impact of the project.

The government conducts periodic evaluations of the projects funded under this scheme.

These evaluations help in assessing the effectiveness of the scheme.

The Sarjansheel Goa scheme is part of a larger framework of cultural grants provided by the state government.

The government encourages feedback from beneficiaries to improve the scheme.

The scheme is expected to evolve based on the changing needs of the cultural sector.

The government aims to increase the budget allocation for the scheme in the coming years.

This increase is intended to support more institutions and larger projects.

The Sarjansheel Goa scheme reflects the government's commitment to cultural preservation and promotion.

It serves as a vital tool for enhancing the cultural landscape of Goa.

The scheme also plays a role in fostering a sense of pride among Goans regarding their cultural heritage.

The government actively promotes this scheme through various outreach programs.

These outreach programs aim to raise awareness about the availability of grants.

The government collaborates with educational institutions to promote cultural projects.

The scheme encourages interdisciplinary projects that combine various forms of art.

Institutions are urged to leverage technology in their projects to reach wider audiences.

The Sarjansheel Goa scheme is an essential component of Goa's cultural policy framework.

It aims to ensure that the rich traditions of Goa are passed on to future generations.

The government is committed to supporting initiatives that enhance the quality of life through culture.

The scheme is a testament to the importance of art and culture in societal development.

The Sarjansheel Goa scheme is a significant step towards recognizing and funding cultural initiatives in the state.
